findings.evidence: Lines 203–241 use the triple only to synthesize the `Fintype`; lines 174–185 use it only through `IsHeckeTriple.mem_of_mem_left`. `TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Basic.lean:223` confirms the triple merely supplies the `Fintype`, while existing APIs such as `Multiplicity/Support.lean:43–44` expose the weaker local `[Finite (DecompQuotient ...)]` convention.
findings.fix: State `heckeSlashSum` and its algebra under `[Finite (DecompQuotient Γ₁ Γ₂ D.out)]` (construct a local `Fintype`), and state the positivity lemmas using direct hypotheses such as `Γ₁ ≤ posDetInt 2` and `D.out ∈ posDetInt 2`; derive the Hecke-triple/`Δ ≤ posDetInt 2` use case at call sites or with a specialized corollary only if needed.
findings.issue: `[IsHeckeTriple Δ Γ₁ Γ₂]` is stronger than every declaration below requires: the sum lemmas need only finiteness of their `DecompQuotient`, while the determinant lemmas use only `Γ₁ ≤ Δ`; `hΔ : Δ ≤ posDetInt 2` also unnecessarily requires every element of `Δ` to be positive rather than just `Γ₁` and `D.out`.

summary: The generalized API still imposes the full Hecke-triple structure where only local finiteness or positivity assumptions are needed.
